channel.title: Star Euthanizer
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Star Euthanizer" - A 2k word draft about a spacecraft and its passenger. Any critique is welcome.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
We talked a bit in IRC for crit on the first two iterations. The third one is going to be a bit more in-depth.

Line by line
That's just fine

SCP-XXXX is presumably made from an alloy of palladium and black rhodium. The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability of acquiring a sample.

This can be one sentence: Although it cannot be confirmed due to the difficulty of acquiring a sample, SCP-XXXX is presumably made from an alloy of palladium and black rhodium.

SCP-XXXX is the object that the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

This seems out of place here, I'd recommend either omitting it (since that's what you imply with the von Zeppelin stuff later) or putting it with the von Zeppelin stuff. It just doesn't seem related to anything else being discussed in this section.

SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity whose age nor origin have been successfully investigated. It claims that these are untraceable because it is a being that was spontaneously formed in the universe.

This is a big deal with part of the reason behind the importance of clinical tone: The Foundation wants to do their best to keep people from getting emotionally attached to anomalies and related beings, so calling it by its preferred name here is a big no-no. I'd recommend this:

"SCP-XXXX-1 is a sapient entity of currently unknown age and origin. During communication with the entity, it has claimed that these details are unknown even to itself, as it was spontaneously formed in the universe."

SCP-XXXX-1 travels through space in search of dying stars. Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will collect the star and store it inside SCP-XXXX. SCP-XXXX-1 has been observed leaping several lightyears worth of distance by Beholder-3. It hasn't elaborated on its way of traveling nor how it can interact with stars. Its whereabouts are currently unknown.

This whole paragraph is a bit haphazardly constructed, and has some issues with tone as well. I'd go with something along the lines of:

"The propulsion method employed by SCP-XXXX is currently unknown. It has been observed by the Beholder-3 satellite to travel several light years nigh instantaneously, and is nearly impossible to track because of this. SCP-XXXX-1 utilizes SCP-XXXX to travel through space in search of dying stars. Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will collect the star and store it inside SCP-XXXX. The entity has not explained the method of propulsion or the mechanism by which it interacts with stars."

Discovery: On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen SCP-XXXX with his telescope. He was administered amnestics, however due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

We discussed this section while talking about its iteration on a previous page, the same comments apply here.

Over the years, von Zeppelin showed more interest in air-travel. After internal discussion, the Foundation decided to allow von Zeppelin to invent new aircraft with undercover personnel beside him as manual laborers. It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX. Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin is the most accurate representation.

A few more issues with tone and structure here.

"Presumably due to the remnants of the memory of SCP-XXXX, von Zeppelin developed a vested interest in air travel. After internal discussion, Foundation administrative staff decided to allow von Zeppelin to create new aircraft with undercover Foundation personnel acting as manual laborers in his employ. It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop an aircraft based on the design of SCP-XXXX. Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin is the most accurate representation, though it is significantly smaller in size."

On 28 August 1903, several researchers observed SCP-XXXX near the Orion Arm and confirmed that this was the same object von Zeppelin saw 30 years ago by its description.

We discussed this section on IRC as well.

On 25 February 1955, the Foundation successfully launched the probes from "The Beholder Line" in space for further research of the universe. On 29 July 1958, SCP-XXXX was observed by Beholder-3 nearly 55 years after its last observation.

I think the quotes around The Beholder Line are unneeded, and it should probably read as 'the Beholder series'. We know the dates involved and can see it was nearly 55 years, so that part is unnecessary.

On 2 July 1962, "The Diplomat", a new probe was launched in space towards Beholder-3 to establish a direct way of communication and give the following objects to the passengers of SCP-XXXX:

  • Several syllabi and audio files of 57 languages.
  • Photographs of life on Earth, and music approved by several site-directors.
  • A transmitter, a receiver, and other equipment

A few minor formatting and tone fixes:

On 2 July 1962, the Diplomat probe was launched in the direction of Beholder-3 with the purpose of establishing a direct line of communication with SCP-XXXX, as well as delivering the following to the passenger(s):

  • Audio files of 57 different Earth languages.
  • Photographs of life on Earth, and music approved by several site directors. (What music?)
  • A transmitter, a receiver, and other equipment

The plural of syllable is syllables, not syllabi. Unless you meant, like, school lesson syllabi, which would be a bit odd since we don't even know if the thing knows our language at all. And why 57 languages specifically? You may want to look into the details of what NASA sent on the gold records put in the Voyager satellites. And what "other equipment" was included? Being so specific in certain regards leads to questions when things like this are left vague. Perhaps just "deep-space radio communication equipment"?

On 14 August 1986, SCP-XXXX-1 answered.

Slight tonal change:

" On 14 August 1986, a response from SCP-XXXX-1 was recorded."

14/08/1986 SCP-XXXX-1:
ARE YOU THERE? BIST DU DA? ÊTES-VOUS LA?

| OTHER LANGUAGES OMITTED FOR BREVITY

Why have three languages displayed, but others omitted? How many languages did it reply with in total? All 57?

Due to the distance and interference, it took each message one week to travel the distance between both parties, full communication logs available below.

More slight tonal changes:

"Due to the distance and interference inherent in deep space radio communication technology, each message took approximately seven days to fully transmit. Full communication logs are available below."

The whole communication log:

This part is definitely an awkward read. I don't know that I want to break it all down individually, but let me lay out a few problems:

  • Something that barely understands our language is giving itself names like The Star Euthanizer and The Pilgrim Between The Suns? Those are not exactly low-level linguistics. Reading on, I can see that it has clearly learned English before, but nobody in the Foundation seems to pick up on this, when at this point in their communication, as far as they know, this is the first time a human has communicated with it. They're not suspicious of this at all?
  • You mention earlier in the article that details like how the ship's propulsion system works are unknown, but nobody seems to be asking anything about the ship here. I'd think that in the 80s, the Foundation would be pretty damn interested in figuring out the mechanics of FTL travel.
  • Why Glen? Is there any significance to that name? Why not send it a list of common Earth names and let it choose one?
  • The Foundation half of the communication feels very informal at times considering that this would presumably be a really big deal. For example: "YOU KNOW THAT DYING STARS ARE HIGHLY EXPLOSIVE, RIGHT?" ", right?" is really informal. "WE DON'T KNOW A LOT ABOUT YOU " should be something like "WE HAVE LITTLE INFORMATION ABOUT YOUR STATUS OR HISTORY". "THEN WHAT AFTER YOU COLLECTED THE LAST ONE?" is another example. These are highly trained, educated, intelligent scientists communicating with an extraterrestrial in deep space, not a few friends catching up over coffee.
  • "I AM THE OLDEST VACUUMBORN BY FAR" he's so old that the concept of time itself is lost to him, but he knows he's the oldest one out there? That seems odd.
  • Him changing his title at the end of every message seems really unnecessary and is just sort of distracting throughout the logs. Didn't he ask to be given a name so that titles and labels wouldn't be used?
  • Why does something as old as time care about wishing humans a happy new year?
  • "YOU HAVE ALWAYS GIVEN ME THE SAME NAME." This thing has reset the universe god knows how many times, but whoever communicates with it always gives it the same name? That's a hell of a coincidence, don't you think?

By an 11:2 vote, it is accepted that SCP-XXXX-1 is responsible for a ZK Universe Reset Scenario but does not directly pose a threat to humanity.

All we have at this point is this thing's word. Even with the technology for FTL travel and containing a star before it goes supernova, there doesn't appear to be any actual evidence that it has the ability to reset the universe. If this was accepted by a vote, I'd think it'd be a much closer ratio than 11:2.

And at the end of it all, why would they not want to contain something with the power to reset the universe? How is that "not directly posing a threat to humanity"??? It may not be attacking us, but resetting the universe is literally the end of the world as we know it. That's not a threat?

The overall idea here is solid, but honestly the article really starts to break down a bit once you get to the communication logs. There's just so much that the Foundation is willing to take at face value when the only solid information they have is pretty limited. There are a myriad of ways it could learn things like the term O5 that don't involve having communicated with the Foundation in a past iteration of the universe, and they just accept that too easily for me to swallow. Unfortunately, I'm not really certain how you'd go about fixing this. I also didn't get much of any emotional response from it, it was more of just an "oh, that's what it's doing." The fact that the spacecraft was the inspiration for the design of the Zeppelin is given great prominence in the earlier iterations, but it seems to end up not really meaning anything besides a one-off line in the communication logs. This is an entity that claims to be as old as time itself and was willed into existence by the universe, and I seem to be more curious about it than the Foundation are.

I guess the best way I can wrap it up is to say that I feel like there's not that much of a narrative here - it's just a list of things happening and a conversation. There wasn't much that made me want to keep reading other than the Zeppelin stuff, and again, that didn't really seem to end up meaning anything.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
{Placeholder}

On to the critique ->
– hide block

SPaG

On 28 August 1903, Foundation personnel educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX through a telescope near the Orion Arm.

This suggests that the telescope was situated in the Orion's Arm spiral arm, rather than the object was located in that sector. Additionally, "astrology" is defined by Merriam-Webster as "the divination of the supposed influences of the stars and planets on human affairs and terrestrial events by their positions and aspects". I believe the word you are looking for is "astronomy".

"sighted" is also defined as "able to see : not blind." Perhaps "observed".

Consistency/Flow

All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This could be cleaned up a bit to be more specific. It is unclear which standard procedure is being followed. Furthermore, I would assume that all deep space observations would be closely monitored by the SCPF as a matter of course.

The production and trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel are present.

This is also jumbled and unclear. What is this meant to prevent?

All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records.

I have a personal preference for utilizing the .aic convention. In this case, your AI would become Binary_Star.aic. I think it looks cleaner than "name", in that it specifies an entity rather than a "supposed" entity. It's all in the implication.

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft ever observed by the Foundation.

Non-human or non-terrestrial? Or did this observation predate Sputnik and the other Earth-based spacecraft?

Closing Remarks

There are significant errors throughout this piece, what is represented here are just a few examples. The idea is a sound one and I think the additional story told throughout the listpages is interesting. However, there are a lot of sentence structure and word choice errors that make this difficult to read.

Ping me on IRC at your leisure and we can go over more of them if you'd like.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
Because Quad has already given you his once over, I will be going more in depth with the tone. I can already say I agree with what Quad has said, so I will be expanding on that. Without further ado!

It's time for some critique.
Hope it helps.

Page one

All telescopes capable of deep-space astrophotography are monitored by satellite following standard procedure.

This sentence reads a little weird to me. I would recommend changing it. Also keep in mind that you will need to change these on the other pages as well.

"All deep-space observatories are to be monitored by satellite following standard procedure."

The production and selling of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is present.

Just a couple of word changes would hep this flow a bit better.

"The production and selling trade of new telescope parts such as refractors have been limited to companies where a sufficient number of undercover Foundation personnel is are present.

All images of SCP-XXXX are intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must be administered Class B amnestics.

Same with this one.

"All images of SCP-XXXX are to be intercepted by the Foundation AI "Binary star", saved in the Foundation database, and subsequently deleted from public records. Witnesses must Those who witness the anomaly are to be administered Class B amnestics.

Page two

The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take a sample.

I would change this slightly.

"The exact composition cannot be confirmed due to the inability to take difficulty in acquiring a sample.

SCP-XXXX is the object where the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

Just one word.

"SCP-XXXX is the object where that the first zeppelin blueprints are based on.

On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a telescope.

I know you said that you would change this, but I think it should stay this way. Adds a bit of historical accuracy that gives this article a nice flavor. There is one change though.

"On 4 December 1872, Ferdinand von Zeppelin claimed to have seen an oblate spheroid spaceship from a with his telescope."

The Foundation administered him with amnestics. Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

This sentence can be structured in a better way.

"The Foundation He was administered him with amnestics. , however due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness."

the Foundation decided to let von Zeppelin invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him as manual laborers.

Some more suggestions.

"the Foundation decided to let allow von Zeppelin to invent new aircraft with undercover personnel besides him planted as manual laborers."

It was anticipated that von Zeppelin eventually would develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX.

I would switch the words ""eventually" and "would" in this sentence.

"It was anticipated that von Zeppelin would eventually develop a scaled-down version of SCP-XXXX."

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX

I feel like you could cut some of this sentence. Sense I would assume researchers searching for SCP-XXXX know a thing or two about astrology.

"On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX-"

Page three

Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1.

"may" doesn't sound very clinical. I would recommend changing this to "are allowed to".

"Personnel with Level 5 Clearance may are allowed to use the Diplomat Terminal to view the communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1.

This can be trimmed down some.

"SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1. SCP-XXXX that serves as a transportation vessel and vault for SCP-XXXX-1."

SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which age nor origin have been successfully investigated.

One word change here.

"SCP-XXXX-1 "Glen" is an entity from which whose age nor origin have been successfully investigated."

-and store it inside of SCP-XXXX.

Don't think the "of" fits there.

"and store it inside of SCP-XXXX."

SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes.

I think you can trim some fat here because you can already infer that SCP-XXXX-1 is knowledgeable about space.

"SCP-XXXX-1 is very knowledgeable about space and space-navigation in general to the extent that it can leap capable of leaping several lightyears worth of distance in mere minutes."

Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal.

Some trimming.

"Due to the distance and interference, it took the message one week to reach Earth/SCP-XXXX-1. Below are the full communication logs with SCP-XXXX-1 from the terminal."

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

| CONNECTION BROKEN MANUALLY
| END HISTORY

I love this. That is why I recommend cutting everything after this. Like Quad said, I like the idea of a good god patrolling space protecting us, but I feel like this would be a far more impactful ending.

All in all I like this article a lot. To answer the questions you proposed on the forum I will say that the 2nd page is fine, your dialogue is great, and I love the twist. The one thing I would recommend thinking about is a way of making the text that has been added over the various iterations of the article pop out more. I have seen articles change the color of new text to blue or red, and I think it could work with this. I would also recommend getting some more critique. This is very close to something great, but there is probably things Quad and I have missed. I hope this was helpful and good luck.

item.title: Re: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

Page 1

SCP-XXXX is the first spacecraft observed by the Foundation.

As in the first ever spacecraft they ever witnessed or just the first one they witnessed for this SCP? Confused by the wording here.

Considering this is a listpages SCP, I know there's more to come and the first page gives so little info, it serves as a good, 'wait, something isn't right…' page, if you know what I mean. Even without the knowledge of listpages, I think it's still just 'off' enough to give the reader the sense that something isn't right.

The clinical is a bit iffy, though. I apologise that I'm doing a more 'general thoughts' crit and not a true in-depth LBL.

Mainly the bits that bothered me were:

new telescope parts like refractors

I feel like 'such as' would be better than 'like'

SCP-XXXX has a frame in the form between a cylinder and an oblate spheroid.

'between a' is what sounds sub-clinical to me. I'm sure there's a better word to use there…sadly, I'm not that great at clinical tone either, so I kinda…can't think of a suitable replacement for that :U

On the bottom side is a small outer room

The adjective 'small' is what bothers me, as I've read somewhere that most adjectives aren't clinical.

Page 2

Immediately, I find myself significantly more intrigued by this page. I know you said you had problems with Page 2, but I really like it so far.

Upon arrival, SCP-XXXX-1 will make said star disappear by unknown means.

'make said star disappear' is vastly unclinical.

How does it make them disappear? By touch?

If so, 'Upon contact with SCP-XXXX-1, stars will immediately vanish. How this occurs is currently unknown.' would be better. But again, I'm no clinical tone pro.

Due to the lesser quality of amnestics at the time, Ferdinand von Zeppelin did not suffer from complete memory-loss and had a few fragments left of SCP-XXXX in his subconsciousness.

That…is such a fucking cool headcanon you thought of. I love this touch. A lot. Zeppelins are the vague hint towards this SCPs existence. I think that's brilliant.

Currently, the LZ 127 Zeppelin represents SCP-XXXX the most accurate.

'Currently, SCP-XXXX is most accurately represented by the LZ 127 Zeppelin.'

On 28 August 1903, several researchers educated in astrology sighted SCP-XXXX near the Orion Arm. Upon showing von Zeppelin their findings, it was confirmed that this was indeed the same object he saw 30 years ago. He was then administered amnestics again, this time resulting in the permanent loss of his memories of SCP-XXXX.

I would just remove this bit. No way the Foundation would show someone an anomaly only to re-amnesticize them again. I don't buy it. Also, we already know that SCP-XXXX is confirmed to be what he saw, so this is unnecessary and repeats info we already know.

Page 2 is pretty good so far. Definitely a good jump from Page 1. I'll go ahead and read Page 3 and I'll let you know how it stacks up.

Page 3

SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger, designated as SCP-XXXX-1 on board

'SCP-XXXX is a dark metallic spacecraft roaming through space with one passenger on board, designated SCP-XXXX-1.'

Also, I really like this bit. This definitely wasn't something I saw coming.

ALSO, HAVE YOU THOUGH OF A NAME YET?

Thought*

YOU HAVE ALWAYS GIVEN ME THE SAME NAME.

- GLEN, SCP-XXXX-1, THE RESETTER OF THE UNIVERSE

That was a twist and a half and I fucking love it and it genuinely gives me motivation to continue my own ambitious as hell listpages SCP.

Thank you for sharing this draft with me.

As for the falling action with the O5 sending Glen the godspeed message…idk how to feel about that.

I really like the idea of an anomaly that can't be contained and is universally recognized as good, but at the same time, idk if this is the most realistic reaction the O5 would have.

Either way, the implications, Glen, and the twist at the end is all superb.

Even with the issues I stated above, that twist at the end would have easily earned my upvote.

I think it all works as a whole, just need polish in all the right areas and you're golden.

I didn't stay to deeply examine the dialogue further, but it's definitely improving significantly.

Either way, I hope I helped. Good luck with the rest of this skip, dude. You got this.

👍

item.title: Star Euthanizer
item.content:encoded:
The draft is about a spacecraft and being roaming trough space and collecting stars. It needs some chipping away for sure. It has 3 list pages (a lot gets repeated but the total word count is 2k).

The main things I want your opinion on

  • Is the second listpage good enough to be there or should I only include the first and last one? Or can I do something better for the transition? Keeping it.
  • Is the dialogue good? The messages take a long time to get an answer in both ways but I want to know if it is good since I am bad at writing dialogue for the most part.
  • Is the twist pulled off successfully?

Anyone reading for specifics only (clinical tone, SP&G,…) is always welcome.

Link to the draft

Thanks in advance.
